resources.desc: OS-level agent harness that compiles a policy DSL to an in-kernel eBPF engine for labeled information-flow control at the syscall boundary, enforcing constraints across any tool or subprocess.

resources.name: Embrace The Red: Offensive BPF!
resources.desc: A series of posts around the introduction into BPF with a focus to an offensive setting, and also how its misuse can be detected. Posts include discussions on the rootkit capabilities of eBPF, or on which tracing type is needed for different use cases.

resources.name: eBPF: Block Linux Fileless Payload "Malware" Execution with BPF LSM
resources.desc: Blog post about how BPF can help detection and blocking fileless malware.

resources.name: Blackhat 2021: With Friends Like eBPF, Who Needs Enemies?
resources.desc: Talk about an eBPF rootkit and how the capabilities of eBPF could be abused. The rootkit was also the object of a talk at Defcon, eBPF, I thought we were friends !.

resources.name: ebpfkit
resources.desc: A rootkit that leverages multiple eBPF features to implement offensive security techniques.

resources.name: ebpfkit-monitor
resources.desc: An utility to statically analyze eBPF bytecode or monitor suspicious eBPF activity at runtime. It was specifically designed to detect ebpfkit.

resources.name: Bad BPF
resources.desc: A collection of malicious eBPF programs that make use of eBPF's ability to read and write user data in between the usermode program and the kernel.

resources.name: TripleCross
resources.desc: A Linux eBPF rootkit with a backdoor, C2, library injection, execution hijacking, persistence and stealth capabilities.

resources.name: linux/include/linux/bpf.h
resources.desc: with linux/include/uapi/bpf.h: definitions related to eBPF, to be used respectively in the kernel and to interface with userspace programs.

resources.name: linux/include/linux/filter.h
resources.desc: with linux/include/uapi/filter.h: information used to run the BPF programs themselves.

resources.name: linux/kernel/bpf/
resources.desc: This directory contains most of BPF-related code. In particular, those files are worth of interest:

resources.name: syscall.c
resources.desc: Different operations permitted by the system call, such as program loading or map management.

resources.name: core.c
resources.desc: BPF interpreter.

resources.name: verifier.c
resources.desc: BPF verifier.

resources.name: linux/net/core/filter.c
resources.desc: Functions and eBPF helpers related to networking (TC, XDP etc.); also contains the code to migrate cBPF bytecode to eBPF (all cBPF programs are translated to eBPF in recent kernels).

resources.name: linux/kernel/trace/bpf_trace.c
resources.desc: Functions and eBPF helpers related to tracing and monitoring (kprobes, tracepoints, etc.).

resources.name: linux/net/sched/
resources.desc: and in particular in files act_bpf.c (action) and cls_bpf.c (filter): code related to BPF actions and filters with TC.

resources.name: linux/net/core/dev.c
resources.desc: contains the function dev_change_xdp_fd() that is called through a Netlink command to hook a XDP program to a device, after is has been loaded into the kernel from user space. This function in turns uses a callback from the relevant driver.

resources.name: The bpf-next tree
resources.desc: BPF patches land in this tree. It is regularly merged into net-next, which is itself merged for each release to Linus' tree.

resources.name: Kernel documentation
resources.desc: About contributions to BPF.

resources.name: The netdev mailing list
resources.desc: Mailing list for Linux kernel networking stack development. All patches are sent there for review and inclusion.

resources.name: XDP-newbies
resources.desc: A mailing list specially dedicated to XDP programming (both for architecture or for asking for help).

resources.name: The XDP Collaboration Project
resources.desc: A GitHub repository with notes and ideas regarding the future evolutions of XDP.
